uncited: The octree represents a volume where each leaf node contains a single scalar datum $v$.
Leaf nodes store a single scalar value $v$.
*   **Cell Primitive:** A box defined by 8 vertices.
The vertices correspond to the centers of 8 adjacent voxels in the octree.
**Logical Shift:** The position of all scalars is logically shifted backward by half a unit of voxel width.
When a ray traverses an octree leaf node at indices $(i, j, k)$ with a datum $v$, the ray intersects a box (cell) where $(i, j, k)$ is mapped to the minimum vertex.
*   For an octree, this requires point location to retrieve the voxel values of the forward neighbors.
*   **Voxel Width:** The unit of voxel width used for the logical shift.
*   **Time Complexity:** Neighbor retrieval in an octree is more intensive than in a 3D array.
